channels.name: main
channels.purpose: Carries all MQTT control packets over an ordered, lossless, bidirectional byte stream.

runtime_implications.summary: A conformant implementation needs a stream transport with in-order, lossless delivery; connectionless transports such as UDP are not suitable on their own.
If MQTT is carried over WebSocket, control packets must be transported in binary frames and packet boundaries cannot be assumed to align with frame boundaries.
Protocol violations and transient processing errors require closing the network connection that carried the offending packet.

roles.name: client
roles.summary: Initiates connections, publishes messages, manages subscriptions, drives keepalive traffic, and participates in QoS acknowledgements.

roles.name: server
roles.summary: Accepts connections, validates control packets, routes published messages to matching subscriptions, manages retained messages and session state, and replies with acknowledgements or connection closure.

interaction_units.name: control_packet
interaction_units.summary: Atomic protocol interaction unit consisting of fixed header, optional variable header, and optional payload.

interaction_units.name: application_message_delivery
interaction_units.summary: Business-level delivery unit carried inside PUBLISH and governed by subscription matching, QoS negotiation, retained-message rules, and session state.

core_flows.name: connection_establishment
core_flows.summary: Client sends CONNECT once per network connection and waits for CONNACK.

core_flows.name: publish_qos0
core_flows.summary: QoS 0 delivery is fire-and-forget: no protocol acknowledgement is exchanged.

core_flows.name: publish_qos1
core_flows.summary: QoS 1 delivery uses PUBLISH followed by PUBACK.

core_flows.name: publish_qos2
core_flows.summary: QoS 2 delivery uses PUBLISH, PUBREC, PUBREL, and PUBCOMP for exactly-once semantics.

core_flows.name: subscription_management
core_flows.summary: Client sends SUBSCRIBE with topic filters and requested QoS; server returns SUBACK with granted result codes.

core_flows.name: unsubscription_management
core_flows.summary: Client sends UNSUBSCRIBE with topic filters; server acknowledges with UNSUBACK.

core_flows.name: keepalive_probe
core_flows.summary: Client uses PINGREQ and expects PINGRESP to verify liveness during quiet periods.

core_flows.name: graceful_disconnect
core_flows.summary: Client sends DISCONNECT to terminate cleanly and suppress Will publication.

surface_catalog.name: CONNECT
surface_catalog.summary: Opens an MQTT session and carries protocol level, client identifier, flags, Keep Alive, optional Will, and optional credentials.

surface_catalog.name: CONNACK
surface_catalog.summary: Acknowledges CONNECT with Session Present flag and a return code.

surface_catalog.name: PUBLISH
surface_catalog.summary: Carries an application message for a Topic Name with DUP, QoS, and RETAIN semantics.

surface_catalog.name: PUBREC
surface_catalog.summary: First acknowledgement of a QoS 2 PUBLISH.

surface_catalog.name: PUBREL
surface_catalog.summary: Release step in QoS 2 flow, sent after PUBREC.

surface_catalog.name: PUBCOMP
surface_catalog.summary: Final acknowledgement of QoS 2 flow after PUBREL.

surface_catalog.name: SUBSCRIBE
surface_catalog.summary: Creates one or more subscriptions with topic filters and requested QoS values.

surface_catalog.name: SUBACK
surface_catalog.summary: Acknowledges SUBSCRIBE with a result code per requested topic filter.

surface_catalog.name: UNSUBSCRIBE
surface_catalog.summary: Removes one or more topic filter subscriptions.

surface_catalog.name: PINGREQ
surface_catalog.summary: Keepalive probe from client to server.

surface_catalog.name: Topic Name
surface_catalog.summary: UTF-8 string naming the concrete publication channel; used in PUBLISH and never contains wildcards.

surface_catalog.name: Topic Filter
surface_catalog.summary: UTF-8 string used in subscriptions and may contain '+' or '#' wildcard syntax.

surface_catalog.name: Packet Identifier
surface_catalog.summary: 16-bit identifier used to correlate QoS 1/2 and subscription acknowledgement flows.

surface_catalog.name: CONNACK return codes
surface_catalog.summary: Connection result codes such as accepted, identifier rejected, bad credentials, and not authorized.

surface_catalog.name: SUBACK return codes
surface_catalog.summary: Per-topic-filter result codes including granted maximum QoS or subscription failure.

message_or_command_entries.name: CONNECT
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header with reserved flags 0000; variable header includes protocol name, protocol level, connect flags, Keep Alive; payload includes Client Identifier and optional Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password.

fields.name: Client Identifier
constraints: must be present in CONNECT payload
zero-byte ClientId is only valid in limited cases defined by server policy and CleanSession semantics

fields.name: Connect Flags
fields.role: encodes CleanSession, Will, Will QoS, Will Retain, User Name, Password
constraints: reserved flag bit must be zero
if Will Flag is 0 then Will Topic and Will Message must be absent and Will QoS must be 0

fields.name: Keep Alive
constraints: 16-bit value
0 disables the keepalive timer semantics

preconditions.summary: Must be the first packet sent by client on a network connection and can only be sent once on that connection.

expected_responses.summary: Server replies with CONNACK indicating acceptance or refusal reason.

state_effects.summary: Creates a new transient session if CleanSession=1, or creates/resumes a persistent session if CleanSession=0.
Arms a Will message on the network connection if Will Flag is set and CONNECT is accepted.

error_paths.condition: Client sends a second CONNECT on the same network connection.
error_paths.required_action: Server must treat this as a protocol violation and close the network connection.

message_or_command_entries.name: CONNACK
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header; variable header contains Session Present flag and Connect Return Code; no payload.

fields.name: Session Present
fields.role: indicates whether an existing persistent session was resumed
constraints: valid only when CleanSession=0 semantics apply

fields.name: Connect Return Code
fields.role: indicates connection acceptance or refusal cause
constraints: must be one of the defined CONNACK codes

preconditions.summary: Sent only in response to CONNECT.

state_effects.summary: Communicates whether the server resumed or created session state.

message_or_command_entries.name: PUBLISH
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header includes DUP, QoS, RETAIN; variable header includes Topic Name and Packet Identifier when QoS>0; payload carries application message bytes.

fields.name: Topic Name
constraints: must be UTF-8
must not contain wildcard characters
present as first field in variable header

fields.name: Packet Identifier
constraints: present only when QoS > 0
must match subsequent acknowledgements

fields.name: RETAIN flag
constraints: RETAIN=1 with non-empty payload stores retained message
RETAIN=1 with zero-byte payload removes retained message and does not store the zero-byte payload

preconditions.summary: If QoS > 0, Packet Identifier must be unused in that sender direction until the exchange completes.

expected_responses.summary: Receiver must send PUBACK for QoS 1.
Receiver must send PUBREC for QoS 2.

state_effects.summary: With QoS 1 or 2, sender stores packet in in-flight session state until acknowledgement completes.
Server dispatches the application message to all matching subscriptions, respecting granted maximum QoS.
With RETAIN=1, server updates retained-message storage for the topic.

error_paths.required_action: Treat packet as protocol-invalid and close the network connection.

message_or_command_entries.name: PUBACK
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header with reserved flags; variable header contains Packet Identifier; no payload.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
fields.role: matches the QoS 1 PUBLISH being acknowledged
constraints: must equal identifier from corresponding PUBLISH

preconditions.summary: Sent only in response to QoS 1 PUBLISH.

state_effects.summary: Completes QoS 1 in-flight state for the corresponding Packet Identifier.

message_or_command_entries.name: PUBREC
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header with reserved flags; variable header contains Packet Identifier; no payload.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
fields.role: matches the QoS 2 PUBLISH being acknowledged
constraints: must equal identifier from corresponding PUBLISH

preconditions.summary: Sent only in response to QoS 2 PUBLISH.

state_effects.summary: Moves QoS 2 sender flow from waiting-for-PUBREC to waiting-for-PUBCOMP after PUBREL is sent.

message_or_command_entries.name: PUBREL
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header has reserved bits 0010; variable header contains Packet Identifier; no payload.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
constraints: must equal identifier from corresponding QoS 2 exchange

preconditions.summary: Sent after PUBREC in QoS 2 flow.

state_effects.summary: Receiver may release duplicate-delivery protection after PUBCOMP is exchanged.

error_paths.condition: PUBREL fixed-header reserved bits are not 0010.
error_paths.required_action: Receiver must treat packet as malformed and close the network connection.

message_or_command_entries.name: PUBCOMP
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header with reserved flags; variable header contains Packet Identifier; no payload.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
fields.role: matches PUBREL in the QoS 2 flow
constraints: must equal identifier from corresponding PUBREL

preconditions.summary: Sent only in response to PUBREL.

state_effects.summary: Completes QoS 2 exchange and clears the in-flight record for that Packet Identifier.

message_or_command_entries.name: SUBSCRIBE
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header reserved bits 0010; variable header contains Packet Identifier; payload contains one or more Topic Filter / Requested QoS pairs.

fields.name: Topic Filter
fields.role: selects matching topics, possibly using wildcards
constraints: must be UTF-8
wildcards are allowed only in Topic Filters

fields.name: Requested QoS
fields.role: requested maximum delivery QoS for each filter
constraints: must be 0, 1, or 2

preconditions.summary: Payload must contain at least one Topic Filter / QoS pair.

expected_responses.summary: Server acknowledges each requested filter with a return code.

state_effects.summary: Adds subscription state to session and may trigger delivery of retained messages for matching topics.

error_paths.condition: Payload is empty or requested QoS uses reserved bits / invalid value.
error_paths.required_action: Server must treat packet as malformed and close the network connection.

message_or_command_entries.name: SUBACK
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header; variable header contains Packet Identifier; payload contains one return code per requested Topic Filter in the original SUBSCRIBE order.

fields.name: Return Codes
fields.role: grant or reject each requested subscription
constraints: must preserve the order of Topic Filters from the SUBSCRIBE request

preconditions.summary: Sent in response to SUBSCRIBE and uses the same Packet Identifier.

message_or_command_entries.name: UNSUBSCRIBE
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header reserved bits 0010; variable header contains Packet Identifier; payload contains one or more Topic Filters.

fields.name: Topic Filter
constraints: payload must contain at least one Topic Filter

state_effects.summary: Removes matching subscription entries from session state.

error_paths.required_action: Server must treat packet as malformed and close the network connection.

message_or_command_entries.name: UNSUBACK
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header; variable header contains Packet Identifier; no payload.

fields.name: Packet Identifier
constraints: must equal identifier from corresponding UNSUBSCRIBE

message_or_command_entries.name: PINGREQ
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header only; no variable header; no payload.

preconditions.summary: Client may send at any time and must send it during inactivity when needed to satisfy Keep Alive.

state_effects.summary: Resets keepalive inactivity detection from the server perspective.

message_or_command_entries.name: PINGRESP
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header only; no variable header; no payload.

state_effects.summary: Lets the client confirm the network connection and server remain responsive.

message_or_command_entries.name: DISCONNECT
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: Fixed header only; no variable header; no payload.

preconditions.summary: Used by client to close connection cleanly.

state_effects.summary: Suppresses Will publication and allows graceful session termination behavior.

shared_fields.name: Remaining Length
shared_fields.summary: Variable-length encoded field in the fixed header giving the number of remaining bytes in the current control packet.
constraints: encoded using 1 to 4 bytes
maximum representable value is 268435455

shared_fields.name: Packet Identifier
shared_fields.summary: Correlates request/acknowledgement pairs and in-flight QoS exchanges.
constraints: 16-bit unsigned integer
sender must not reuse while exchange is incomplete

shared_fields.name: Topic Name and Topic Filter strings
shared_fields.summary: UTF-8 encoded protocol strings used for routing and subscription matching.
constraints: encoded length must not exceed 65535 bytes
Topic Names must not contain wildcards
Topic Filters may use '+' and '#'

global_framing_rules.summary: Every control packet consists of a fixed header and may also contain a variable header and/or payload depending on packet type.
Fixed-header low bits contain type-specific flags; where the specification fixes reserved values, invalid values are fatal protocol violations.
PUBLISH is the only control packet that carries application message payloads; all other business behavior is expressed through control flow packets and subscription metadata.

entries.name: 0x04
entries.meaning: Connection Refused, bad user name or password

state_scopes.name: network_connection
state_scopes.summary: TCP/WebSocket connection on which MQTT control packets flow and to which Keep Alive and Will arming are attached.

state_scopes.name: session
state_scopes.summary: Longer-lived state that may span network reconnections when CleanSession=0.

state_scopes.name: packet_exchange
state_scopes.summary: In-flight state for QoS 1 and QoS 2 packet identifiers and handshakes.

state_objects.name: session
state_objects.summary: Contains subscriptions, unacknowledged QoS messages, and session existence metadata.

state_objects.name: will_message_binding
state_objects.summary: Stores the Will Message associated with an accepted CONNECT until DISCONNECT or abnormal connection end.

state_objects.name: inflight_qos_records
state_objects.summary: Tracks sender/receiver progress for QoS 1 and QoS 2 packet identifiers.

state_nodes.name: connection_open_uninitialized
state_nodes.summary: Network connection exists but CONNECT has not yet been processed.

state_nodes.name: connected_clean_session
state_nodes.summary: Accepted connection with CleanSession=1 using transient session state tied to the current network connection.

state_nodes.name: connected_persistent_session
state_nodes.summary: Accepted connection with CleanSession=0, using resumed or newly created persistent session state.

state_nodes.name: will_armed
state_nodes.summary: Will message is associated with the connection and will be published on abnormal termination.

state_nodes.name: qos1_inflight
state_nodes.summary: QoS 1 PUBLISH has been sent and awaits PUBACK.

state_nodes.name: qos2_wait_pubrec
state_nodes.summary: QoS 2 PUBLISH sent and awaiting PUBREC.

state_nodes.name: qos2_wait_pubcomp
state_nodes.summary: QoS 2 PUBREL sent and awaiting PUBCOMP.

transitions.name: accept_clean_session_zero
conditions: CONNECT is syntactically valid and accepted
actions: resume an existing session if it exists, otherwise create a new persistent session
set Session Present in CONNACK according to whether the session existed
retained_data_effects: persistent session state is associated with the current network connection

transitions.name: accept_clean_session_one
conditions: CONNECT is syntactically valid and accepted
actions: discard any previous session state for this client identifier
start a new transient session for the current network connection
cleanup_effects: previous persistent session state is deleted

transitions.name: arm_will_after_connect
actions: store Will Message and bind it to the network connection
retained_data_effects: Will Message is stored until DISCONNECT or abnormal termination

transitions.name: keepalive_timeout_disconnect
transitions.trigger: No control packet received within 1.5 × Keep Alive interval

transitions.name: reconnect_with_unacknowledged_state
transitions.trigger: Client reconnects with CleanSession=0 after prior disconnect
conditions: unacknowledged QoS 1 or QoS 2 state exists
actions: client and server re-send unacknowledged PUBLISH and PUBREL packets using original Packet Identifiers

timers_and_constants.name: keep_alive_interval
timers_and_constants.value_or_rule: Client-specified 16-bit seconds value; 0 disables keepalive semantics.

timers_and_constants.name: server_keep_alive_enforcement
timers_and_constants.value_or_rule: Server must disconnect if it receives no control packet within 1.5 times the Keep Alive value when Keep Alive is non-zero.

retained_data.name: session_transient_state
retained_data.summary: Subscriptions and in-flight QoS state for CleanSession=1, valid only for the current network connection.

retained_data.name: session_persistent_state
retained_data.summary: Subscriptions and unacknowledged QoS state that survive disconnection when CleanSession=0.

retained_data.name: will_message
retained_data.summary: Message published on abnormal connection end unless removed by DISCONNECT.

retained_data.name: inflight_qos_records
retained_data.summary: Outstanding QoS 1/2 sends and receives tracked by Packet Identifier.

cleanup_rules.name: disconnect_with_cleansession_one
cleanup_rules.summary: When CleanSession=1, both client and server discard session state at connection end.

cleanup_rules.name: disconnect_with_cleansession_zero
cleanup_rules.summary: When CleanSession=0, subscriptions and unacknowledged QoS state are preserved, but network-connection-scoped state is discarded.

dispatch_keys.name: topic_name
dispatch_keys.summary: Published message routing key used to find matching subscriptions.

dispatch_keys.name: topic_filter
dispatch_keys.summary: Subscription-side matching expression, possibly containing '+' or '#'.

dispatch_targets.name: matching_subscriptions
dispatch_targets.summary: Server dispatches an application message to every subscription whose Topic Filter matches the Topic Name.

dispatch_targets.name: session_queue
dispatch_targets.summary: For offline or persistent sessions, server can store matching QoS 1/2 messages in session state for later delivery.

matching_rules.summary: Topic Names must not contain wildcards; '+' and '#' are valid only in Topic Filters.
The multi-level wildcard '#' must be either alone or follow a topic separator and must be the final character in the filter.
The single-level wildcard '+' must occupy an entire topic level.
Matching is character-for-character by topic level; server must not normalize topic names or filters.
Topic Filters starting with a wildcard do not match Topic Names beginning with '$'.

resource_objects.name: topic_resource
creation_rules: may be predefined by server administrator
may be dynamically created on first subscription or first application message publication
lifetime_rules: exists as long as server chooses to maintain it

resource_objects.name: subscription
lifetime_rules: exists until removed by UNSUBSCRIBE, session deletion, or connection end when CleanSession=1

resource_objects.name: retained_message
creation_rules: created or replaced when server receives PUBLISH with RETAIN=1 and non-empty payload
lifetime_rules: persists independently of session lifetime until replaced or deleted
deletion_rules: PUBLISH with RETAIN=1 and zero-byte payload for same topic

resource_objects.name: session_state
creation_rules: created on accepted CONNECT when no existing session is resumed

lifecycle_rules.summary: A topic resource may be predefined or dynamically created on first matching use; the protocol does not define garbage-collection rules for unused topic resources.
Retained messages persist independently of session state and are delivered to newly created matching subscriptions.
Subscriptions are session-scoped: transient for CleanSession=1 and persistent for CleanSession=0.

persistence_scope.name: retained_message_store
persistence_scope.summary: Retained messages survive session end and are not part of session state.

persistence_scope.name: persistent_session_state
persistence_scope.summary: Subscriptions and in-flight QoS data persist across reconnect only when CleanSession=0.

ownership_and_authority.summary: Server may use a security component to selectively authorize operations on a topic resource for a given client.
Server owns retained-message storage and applies RETAIN semantics on PUBLISH processing.

storage_requirements.summary: Server must store retained message payload and QoS when RETAIN=1 and payload is non-empty.
Server must not store a zero-byte retained message; instead it removes any existing retained message for that topic.
For CleanSession=0, server stores subscriptions and unacknowledged QoS 1/2 state across disconnections.

business_operations.name: publish_application_message
business_operations.summary: Accepts an application message on a Topic Name, applies QoS and RETAIN semantics, and dispatches to matching subscribers.

business_operations.name: create_subscription
business_operations.summary: Adds one or more Topic Filters to session state and negotiates maximum QoS for each.

business_operations.name: remove_subscription
business_operations.summary: Removes Topic Filter entries from session state.

error_matrix.condition: A control packet is received with invalid fixed-header reserved bits for its packet type.
error_matrix.state_cleanup: Discard connection-scoped state; Will handling follows abnormal disconnect semantics if applicable.

error_matrix.condition: SUBSCRIBE payload is empty or Requested QoS contains reserved / invalid value.
error_matrix.required_action: Treat packet as malformed and close the network connection.
error_matrix.state_cleanup: Do not create subscription state for the invalid request.

error_matrix.required_action: Treat packet as malformed and close the network connection.

error_matrix.condition: Client sends a second CONNECT packet on the same network connection.
error_matrix.required_action: Treat as protocol violation and disconnect the client.
error_matrix.state_cleanup: Current connection is terminated; persistent session handling follows disconnect semantics.

error_matrix.condition: Control packet contains ill-formed UTF-8 or a UTF-8 string containing U+0000.
error_matrix.state_cleanup: Discard connection-scoped state; persistent session policy follows disconnect semantics.

error_matrix.condition: Keep Alive is non-zero and server receives no control packet within the allowed interval.
error_matrix.state_cleanup: Connection-scoped state is removed; Will Message is published if armed.

error_matrix.condition: Client does not receive PINGRESP within a reasonable time after PINGREQ.
error_matrix.state_cleanup: Connection-scoped state is removed locally; reconnect policy is implementation-controlled.

configurable_bounds.name: keep_alive_interval
configurable_bounds.value_or_rule: application-specific 16-bit seconds value; 0 disables keepalive semantics

base_protocol_requirements.summary: Authentication and authorization decisions are server-controlled and reflected in CONNECT/CONNACK processing and topic-resource authorization policy.

recommended_practices.summary: Server implementations that offer TLS should use TCP port 8883.

external_security_dependencies.name: TLS
external_security_dependencies.summary: Transport confidentiality and peer protection are provided by TLS rather than by core MQTT packet semantics.

explicitly_out_of_scope_security_feature.summary: The core MQTT 3.1.1 document does not define an application-layer encryption or message-signing scheme beyond transport security.

out_of_scope_candidates.summary: Administrative policies for session eviction and topic-resource garbage collection are intentionally implementation-defined.

must_support_surface.name: CONNECT
must_support_surface.reason: Connection establishment is mandatory for every MQTT session.

must_support_surface.name: CONNACK
must_support_surface.reason: Connection acceptance/refusal must be expressed through CONNACK.

must_support_surface.name: PUBLISH
must_support_surface.reason: Carries application messages and retained-message semantics.

must_support_surface.name: PINGREQ
must_support_surface.reason: Needed to support keepalive behavior on otherwise idle connections.

must_support_surface.name: PINGRESP
must_support_surface.reason: Required reply for keepalive probe handling.

must_support_surface.name: DISCONNECT
must_support_surface.reason: Supports graceful shutdown and Will suppression.

must_support_state_behaviors.summary: Must implement CleanSession handling for creating, resuming, and discarding session state.
Must track keepalive timeout and connection liveness behavior.
Must support in-flight QoS 1 and QoS 2 tracking if QoS 1/2 PUBLISH is in scope.

may_defer_features.summary: A minimal broker may defer WebSocket transport support and implement only raw TCP initially.
A minimal implementation may defer advanced authorization policy engines while still obeying the protocol surface.

implementation_assumptions.summary: Underlying transport is TCP or an equivalent ordered, lossless, bidirectional stream transport.
The implementation models topic matching and retained-message storage on the server side.

planning_checklist: 报文模型与编解码范围
implementation_risks: MQTT 的协议表面覆盖面较大，14 类 control packet 需要统一编解码框架而不是零散处理。
CleanSession、Will、Keep Alive、QoS 1/2 会引入跨连接和跨报文的状态耦合。
Topic Filter 匹配与 retained-message 生命周期决定了 router 和 resource 层都不能省略。
协议错误处理以“关闭连接”为主，但仍需区分 malformed packet、超时、认证拒绝和会话恢复等路径。
planning_inputs.protocol_summary: MQTT 的工程规划必须同时覆盖完整 control packet surface、session/state 语义、topic-based routing、retained storage 和严格的错误关闭策略。
critical_stateful_behaviors: CleanSession=0 时恢复或创建持久会话并设置 Session Present。
CleanSession=1 时丢弃任何旧会话并建立瞬时会话。
Keep Alive 超时导致断开连接，并在 Will 已绑定时发布 Will Message。
QoS 1/2 的 Packet Identifier 不能在交换完成前复用。
断线重连时，CleanSession=0 必须重发未确认的 PUBLISH 和 PUBREL。
error_handling_obligations: invalid fixed-header reserved bits -> close network connection
empty SUBSCRIBE / invalid Requested QoS -> close network connection
empty UNSUBSCRIBE payload -> close network connection
second CONNECT on same network connection -> disconnect client
ill-formed UTF-8 or embedded null -> close network connection
Keep Alive timeout -> disconnect client and publish Will if armed
persistence_and_lifecycle_obligations: Persistent session state survives reconnect only when CleanSession=0.
Retained messages are not part of session state and persist until replaced or deleted.
Subscriptions are session-scoped and removed by UNSUBSCRIBE or session deletion.
Topic resources may be predefined or dynamically created; garbage collection policy is implementation-defined.

consistency_findings.summary: All interaction flows map to explicit control packets in message_model.
minimum_v1 references surface units and obligations that are represented in the main facts.

coverage_gaps.summary: Administrative policies for deleting idle topic resources are not standardized by MQTT 3.1.1.
Transport security is externalized to TLS and deployment policy rather than defined purely in packet semantics.

open_questions.question: What concrete garbage-collection policy should an implementation apply to dynamically created topic resources with no subscriptions and no retained message?
open_questions.suggested_followup: Choose an implementation policy and document it as a broker-specific behavior.

open_questions.question: How should persistent session state be bounded or evicted under resource pressure while remaining compliant with CleanSession=0 semantics?
open_questions.suggested_followup: Define broker resource quotas and eviction/administrative cleanup rules.

open_questions.question: Which TLS profile, credential model, and topic-level authorization mechanism should the implementation require in its target deployment?
open_questions.suggested_followup: Select deployment security requirements outside the MQTT 3.1.1 core packet model.

evidence_index.excerpt: The protocol runs over TCP/IP, or over other network protocols that provide ordered, lossless, bi-directional connections.
A conformant Server MUST support the use of one or more underlying transport protocols that provide an ordered, lossless, stream of bytes from the Client to Server and Server to Client.

evidence_index.section_hint: 6 Using WebSocket as a network transport
evidence_index.excerpt: MQTT Control Packets MUST be sent in WebSocket binary data frames... The receiver MUST NOT assume that MQTT Control Packets are aligned on WebSocket frame boundaries.

evidence_index.section_hint: Appendix B. Mandatory normative statements (non normative)
evidence_index.excerpt: Unless stated otherwise, if either the Server or Client encounters a protocol violation, it MUST close the Network Connection...
MQTT Control Packet: A packet of information that is sent across the Network Connection. The MQTT specification defines fourteen different types of Control Packet...

evidence_index.section_hint: 3.1 CONNECT – Client requests a connection to a Server
evidence_index.excerpt: The CONNECT Packet is sent from the Client to the Server to request a connection.
The CONNACK Packet is sent by the Server in response to a CONNECT Packet received from a Client.

evidence_index.section_hint: 4. Start message delivery and keep alive monitoring.
evidence_index.excerpt: An Application Message is sent to each Client Subscription whose Topic Filter matches the Topic Name attached to an Application Message.

evidence_index.section_hint: 3.1 CONNECT – Client requests a connection to a Server
evidence_index.excerpt: After sending a CONNECT Packet, the Client MUST wait for a CONNACK Packet from the Server.
QoS 0: at most once delivery.
The receiver of a QoS 1 PUBLISH Packet MUST respond with a PUBACK Packet.

evidence_index.section_hint: 3.5 PUBREC – Publish received (QoS 2 publish received, part 1)
evidence_index.excerpt: QoS 2 delivery uses a four-phase handshake: PUBLISH -> PUBREC -> PUBREL -> PUBCOMP.
When the Server receives a SUBSCRIBE Packet from a Client, the Server MUST respond with a SUBACK Packet.
The Server MUST respond to an UNSUBSCRIBE request with an UNSUBACK Packet.
The Client can send PINGREQ at any time... and use PINGRESP to determine that the network and the Server are responsive.
The DISCONNECT Packet is sent from the Client to the Server to indicate that it is disconnecting cleanly.
Each MQTT Control Packet contains a fixed header, and some packet types contain a variable header and a payload.
The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme and can use up to four bytes.
The Packet Identifier field is only present in PUBLISH Packets where the QoS level is 1 or 2... SUBACK and UNSUBACK MUST contain the Packet Identifier used in the corresponding request.

evidence_index.section_hint: 3.1 CONNECT – Client requests a connection to a Server
evidence_index.excerpt: The CONNECT Packet variable header contains Protocol Name, Protocol Level, Connect Flags, and Keep Alive; the payload contains Client Identifier and optional Will/User Name/Password.
Byte 1 is the Connect Acknowledge Flags... Bit 0 is the Session Present Flag. Byte 2 is the Connect Return Code.
The Topic Name MUST be present as the first field in the PUBLISH Packet Variable header... The Topic Name MUST NOT contain wildcard characters.
PUBACK contains the Packet Identifier of the PUBLISH Packet that is being acknowledged.

evidence_index.section_hint: 3.5 PUBREC – Publish received (QoS 2 publish received, part 1)
evidence_index.excerpt: PUBREC is the response to a PUBLISH Packet with QoS 2.
Bits 3,2,1 and 0 of the fixed header in the PUBREL Control Packet are reserved and MUST be set to 0,0,1 and 0 respectively.
PUBCOMP is the response to a PUBREL Packet.
The SUBSCRIBE Packet is sent from the Client to the Server to create one or more Subscriptions.

Each return code corresponds to a Topic Filter in the SUBSCRIBE Packet being acknowledged. The order of return codes in the SUBACK Packet MUST match the order of Topic Filters in the SUBSCRIBE Packet.
The payload of an UNSUBSCRIBE packet contains the Topic Filters that the Client wishes to unsubscribe from.
The UNSUBACK Packet has no payload.
The PINGREQ Packet is sent from a Client to the Server and can be used to indicate that the Client is alive.
PINGRESP is sent by the Server to the Client in response to a PINGREQ Packet.
The DISCONNECT Packet is sent from the Client to the Server to indicate that it is disconnecting cleanly.
Topic Names and Topic Filters are UTF-8 encoded strings... Topic Names MUST NOT include wildcard characters.
If the Server rejects the ClientId it MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02...
Allowed return codes: 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x80.
If CleanSession is set to 0, the Server MUST resume communications with the Client based on state from the current Session... If there is no Session ... the Server MUST create a new Session.
If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one.
If the Will Flag is set to 1... a Will Message MUST be stored on the Server and associated with the Network Connection... deleted on receipt of a DISCONNECT Packet.
If the Keep Alive value is non-zero and the Server does not receive a Control Packet from the Client within one and a half times the Keep Alive time period, it MUST disconnect the Network Connection.
When a Client reconnects with CleanSession set to 0, both the Client and Server MUST re-send any unacknowledged PUBLISH Packets and PUBREL Packets using their original Packet Identifiers.

The Session state in the Server consists of the existence of a Session, the Client's subscriptions, QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages sent but not acknowledged, QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages pending transmission...
An Application Message is sent to each Client Subscription whose Topic Filter matches the Topic Name attached to an Application Message.
The wildcard characters can be used in Topic Filters, but MUST NOT be used within a Topic Name.
The multi-level wildcard character MUST be specified either on its own or following a topic level separator... The single-level wildcard ... MUST occupy an entire level of the filter.

The Server MUST NOT perform any normalization of Topic Names or Topic Filters... Each non-wildcarded level in the Topic Filter has to match the corresponding level in the Topic Name character for character.
The Server MUST NOT match Topic Filters starting with a wildcard character (# or +) with Topic Names beginning with a $ character.

The topic resource MAY be either predefined in the Server by an administrator or it MAY be dynamically created by the Server when it receives the first subscription or an Application Message with that Topic Name.
If the RETAIN flag is set to 1... the Server MUST store the Application Message and its QoS... A zero byte retained message MUST NOT be stored as a retained message on the Server.
The SUBSCRIBE Packet creates one or more Subscriptions... UNSUBSCRIBE removes Topic Filters that the Client wishes to unsubscribe from.
After the disconnection of a Session that had CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST store further QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages that match any subscriptions.
A PUBLISH Packet with a RETAIN flag set to 1 and a payload containing zero bytes... any existing retained message with the same topic name MUST be removed.
If invalid flags are received, the receiver MUST close the Network Connection.

The payload of a SUBSCRIBE packet MUST contain at least one Topic Filter / QoS pair... the Server MUST treat a SUBSCRIBE packet as malformed and close the Network Connection if Requested QoS is not 0,1 or 2.
An UNSUBSCRIBE packet with no payload is a protocol violation.

evidence_index.section_hint: 3.1 CONNECT – Client requests a connection to a Server
evidence_index.excerpt: A Client can only send the CONNECT Packet once over a Network Connection. The Server MUST process a second CONNECT Packet sent from a Client as a protocol violation and disconnect the Client.
If a Server or Client receives a Control Packet containing ill-formed UTF-8... or containing U+0000 it MUST close the Network Connection.
If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId with CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST respond with a CONNACK return code 0x02 and then close the Network Connection.

If the Keep Alive value is non-zero and the Server does not receive a Control Packet... it MUST disconnect the Network Connection. If a Client does not receive a PINGRESP... it SHOULD close the Network Connection.
The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four and the maximum value is 268435455.
Topic Names and Topic Filters are UTF-8 encoded strings, they MUST NOT encode to more than 65535 bytes.
A Keep Alive value of zero (0) has the effect of turning off the keep alive mechanism.
Server implementations that offer TLS SHOULD use TCP port 8883.
The Server MAY also use a security component to selectively authorize actions on the topic resource for a given Client.
